deep.reconstruction:
Folio 67r is the opening page of the draft of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift (submitted 1853, read 1854, published by Dedekind in 1867 as 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe'). The draft title here is 'Über die Fourier'schen Reihen'. The page has no derivations of its own. It contains the introduction and the start of Section I, the historical part.

(a) Plan of the essay. It will give first a history of the subject, compiled with Dirichlet's guidance. It will then examine the cases excluded from earlier work, namely functions not covered by Dirichlet's conditions.

(b) Definition of a Fourier series:
sum_{n>=1} a_n sin(nx) + b_0/2 + sum_{n>=1} b_n cos(nx).
Riemann adds the remark that progress in the mathematics of 'quite arbitrary functions', so important for physics, depended on insight into these series.

(c) The historical problem. The question of representing an arbitrary function by such a series first arose in the mid-18th century, in the controversy over the vibrating string.
- Modern statement: the transverse displacement y(x,t) of a uniform string satisfies y_tt = alpha^2 y_xx (eq. (1)). Here alpha is independent of t, and also of x if the string has uniform thickness.
- d'Alembert (Berlin Mémoires 1747, p. 214) showed that every solution has the form y = f(x + alpha t) + phi(x - alpha t).
- The sentence continues on the next page ('enthalten sein müsste').
- The justification also comes on the next page. In characteristic coordinates p = x + alpha t, q = x - alpha t, the operator becomes a multiple of the mixed derivative y_pq. Hence y_pq = 0 and y = f(p) + phi(q).
- [My completion:] y_x = y_p + y_q and y_t = alpha(y_p - y_q), so y_tt - alpha^2 y_xx = -4 alpha^2 y_pq.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; the wave equation and d'Alembert's general solution are stated correctly.

Bibliographic: the in-text citation 'Hist. de l'ac. Roy. d. sc. et b. l. 1747 p. 214' and the margin note 'Mémoires de l'académie de Berlin 1747 pag 214' refer to the same volume. The published 1867 text uses the 'Mémoires de l'académie de Berlin' form.

Context only (next page, not this one): the identity y_tt - alpha^2 y_xx = d/d(x-alpha t)(dy/d(x+alpha t)) omits the factor -4 alpha^2. Riemann's own side computation (1/4 y_xx - 1/(4 alpha^2) y_tt = y_pq) is correct, and the printed version carries -4 alpha^2 as far as I recall. The omission is harmless for the conclusion y_pq = 0.

The only novelties are minor textual variants, such as the draft title 'Über die Fourier'schen Reihen' and wording differences.
